section_summary: This section documents State Department and inter-agency deliberations from March through May 1947 regarding U.S. economic policy toward occupied Japan, concentrating on deconcentration of excessive economic power (the anti-Zaibatsu program) and plans to revive Japanese foreign trade. Officials including Edwin M. Martin, Seymour J. Rubin, and Robert W. Barnett debated proposals to 'crank up' Japanese industrial production through revolving credit funds and raw material imports, balancing the desire to relieve U.S. occupation costs against the geopolitical concerns of wartime Asian allies. The records also include Far Eastern Commission policy implementations, SWNCC decisions (particularly SWNCC 302 series), directives on short-period controls, and communications with SCAP regarding trade missions and domestic controls.

subfiles.about: Provides legal commentary and recommended revisions on the proposed policy paper concerning the dissolution of excessive concentrations of economic power and Zaibatsu restrictions in Japan.
subfiles.from: Seymour J. Rubin
subfiles.summary: Rubin critiques definitions of excessive concentration, noting German decartelization precedents and the Sherman Act. He suggests limiting officer/director bans to ten years, revising compensation and asset-blocking mechanisms for Zaibatsu individuals, exempting non-Zaibatsu persons, and eliminating arbitrary post-dissolution financial penalties.
subfiles.title: Legal Comments on the Proposed Policy Concerning Excessive Concentrations of Economic Power in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits proposed amendments to the SWNCC paper on excessive concentrations of economic power in Japan for legal review.
subfiles.from: C.R.S. (Office of the Legal Adviser)
subfiles.summary: Transmits proposed SWNCC paper amendments to Fahy, noting Rubin is securing a copy to compare with his recommendations.
subfiles.title: Note to the Legal Adviser Regarding Proposed Amendments to SWNCC Paper on Excessive Concentrations of Economic Power in Japan

subfiles.about: Presents specific text amendments to the conclusions and articles of the SWNCC paper on excessive concentrations of economic power in Japan.
subfiles.from: Office of the Legal Adviser, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Proposes ten specific amendments to the SWNCC paper, clarifying SCAP's schedule of restricted concerns, standardizing criteria for associates acting on behalf of Zaibatsu figures, adjusting compensation rules to prevent revival of Zaibatsu power, and safeguarding United Nations and neutral interests.
subfiles.title: Proposed Amendments to SWNCC Paper on Excessive Concentrations of Economic Power in Japan

subfiles.about: Notifies SCAP of FEC policy on short period Japanese economic controls to relieve world shortages and reports on FEC voting on advance reparations transfers.
subfiles.from: Department of State (George C. Marshall)
subfiles.summary: Informs SCAP that the FEC adopted a policy requiring Japanese production of consumption goods to relieve world shortages while restricting domestic consumption. Also reports that six countries support and three oppose the U.S. proposal for advance transfers of Japanese reparations.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Telegram No. 70 to SCAP Tokyo on Short Period Controls Over Japanese Economy and Advance Transfers of Reparations
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits an intelligence memorandum estimating Japanese domestic consumption and balances of payments for 1948, 1950, and 1952.
subfiles.from: Warren S. Hunsberger (Division of Research for Far East)
subfiles.summary: Transmits Intelligence Memorandum OIR No. 3436.95, prepared by DRF at the request of Martin's division.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Intelligence Memorandum No. 3436.95 on Japan's Domestic Consumption and Balances of Payments
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin (Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs)

subfiles.about: Presents detailed statistical projections and balance-of-payments estimates for post-war Japan covering the years 1948, 1950, and 1952.
subfiles.from: Japan Branch, Division of Research for Far East, Office of Intelligence Research
subfiles.summary: This intelligence report provides statistical projections and balance-of-payments models for post-war Japan covering the years 1948, 1950, and 1952 compared to 1930-1934 baselines. It analyzes per capita consumption of key commodities including foodstuffs, textiles, finished steel, timber, and coal. Detailed import and export schedules outline the requirements to 'crank up' the Japanese economy and achieve viable self-sufficiency by 1950.
subfiles.title: Intelligence Memorandum OIR No. 3436.95: Estimate of Japan's Domestic Consumption and Balances of Payments in 1948, 1950 and 1952

subfiles.about: Proposes a comprehensive economic program to make Japan self-supporting by 1950, end U.S. relief expenditures, and facilitate reparations.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin (Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Proposes an economic program for Japan integrating the Reparations Policy Committee report and import-export projections. Recommends 'cranking up' Japanese production through expanded raw material imports financed via revolving funds, promoting private trade, repaying U.S. advances from export proceeds, and offering current reparations credits to Far Eastern allies.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on a Positive Economic Program for Japan
subfiles.to: John H. Hilldring (Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas)

subfiles.about: Presents a detailed policy analysis proposing the revitalization of the Japanese economy, import-export financing, administrative controls, and reparations.
subfiles.from: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs (Edwin M. Martin)
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive policy paper analyzes the imperative of reviving the Japanese economy to end U.S. relief costs and support Asian economic recovery. It calculates that pump-priming imports of food and industrial raw materials in 1948-1949 can restore self-sufficiency by 1950 without expanding deficits. The paper addresses auxiliary problems including dollar shortages, weak Japanese ministries, SCAP administrative leadership, and overcoming the resistance of Far Eastern nations by offering current reparations credits.
subfiles.title: A Positive Economic Program for Japan

subfiles.about: Circulates the proposed economic revival program to Department divisions and advises caution regarding Assistant Secretary Peterson's planned mission to Japan.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin (Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Circulates the economic revival program and advises awaiting SCAP views and Whitman's return before dispatching Peterson's proposed interdepartmental mission.
subfiles.title: Cover Memorandum Circulating the Positive Economic Program for Japan
subfiles.to: John H. Hilldring (Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas)

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of JCS Directive Serial No. 70 to SCAP regarding short period economic controls for transmittal to the FEC and State Department files.
subfiles.from: H. W. Moseley (Secretary, SWNCC)
subfiles.summary: Transmits three copies of JCS Directive Serial No. 70 to SCAP for transmittal to the FEC and departmental files.
subfiles.title: SWN-5296: Directive Transmitted to SCAP by the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (Attention: J. L. Penfield, FE)

subfiles.about: Directs SCAP to implement FEC policy on short period controls over the Japanese economy to maximize export production and limit domestic consumption.
subfiles.from: Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.summary: Instructs SCAP to implement FEC policy by maximizing Japanese production of essential goods (such as textiles and light manufactures) to relieve world shortages, while restricting Japanese domestic per capita textile consumption to 2.5 pounds per year plus limited incentive allowances.
subfiles.title: Directive Serial No. 70: Short Period Controls Over the Japanese Economy to Relieve World Shortages
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's reply to the JCS directive regarding FEC short period economic controls.
subfiles.from: H. W. Moseley (Secretary, SWNCC)
subfiles.summary: Transmits SCAP's message CM-IN-2343 replying to the directive on short-period economic controls for State Department information and action.
subfiles.title: SWN-5230: Draft Directive Regarding Short Period Controls over the Japanese Economy to Relieve World Shortages

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the FEC directive on economic controls and cautions against rigid quantitative limitations in overall policy.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo
subfiles.summary: SCAP acknowledges the directive on short-period controls, states all features are already anticipated and in effect, but advises that quantitative policy limitations should be avoided or carefully verified with SCAP in advance.
subfiles.title: Incoming Classified Message C-50837 from SCAP on FEC Directive on Short Period Controls
subfiles.to: War Department for Joint Chiefs of Staff

subfiles.about: Informs the U.S. Member of the Far Eastern Commission of SCAP's response regarding the directive on short period economic controls.
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring (Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas)
subfiles.summary: Transmits the text of SCAP's March 13 message acknowledging Directive Serial No. 70 and cautioning against quantitative limitations in FEC overall policy.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the United States Member, Far Eastern Commission Regarding SCAP's Message on Short Period Controls
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Records the withdrawal and charge-out of classified document 894.50/3-2547 from Department files.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Official charge-out sheet (Form DS-933a) for secret document 894.50/3-2547, recorded on January 22, 1953.
subfiles.title: Department of State Cross-Reference / Withdrawal Sheet for File 894.50/3-2547

subfiles.about: Submits State Department amendments to SWNCC 302/2 regarding the deconcentration and public regulation of Japanese monopolies.
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring (State Department Member, SWNCC)
subfiles.summary: Hilldring submits proposed amendments to SWNCC 302/2, arguing that public regulation or ownership of technologically indivisible monopolies should be mandatory rather than permissive, defining regulatory safeguards against bureaucratic abuse, and warning against mixed public-private enterprises.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Secretary, SWNCC: U.S. Policy With Respect to Excessive Concentrations of Economic Power in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits background materials on Japanese labor movements, wages, and the textile industry to Killen prior to his departure for Japan.
subfiles.from: Warren S. Hunsberger (Chief, Japan Branch, Division of Research for Far East)
subfiles.summary: Transmits State Department and SCAP reports on Japanese labor movements, wage tables, and the textile industry to Killen ahead of his assignment in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Speedletter Transmitting Background Information on Japanese Labor and Textile Industry

subfiles.about: Discusses trade financing, reopening private trade, revolving credit funds, appropriations, food problems, and SCAP leadership over economic controls.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman (Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Whitman discusses informal policy coordination, outlining plans to leverage $100 million in Japanese liquid funds into $400-500 million in credit for raw materials. He discusses opening private trade by August 1, Congressional budget hearings, and welcomes MacArthur's renewed initiative on domestic economic controls.
subfiles.title: Informal Letter to Brigadier General W. F. Marquat on Japanese Economic Programs and Trade Financing
subfiles.to: Brigadier General William F. Marquat (Chief, ESS, SCAP)

subfiles.about: Transmits approved SWNCC 302/2 for submission of Appendix C to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring (Chairman, SWNCC)
subfiles.summary: Transmits approved SWNCC 302/2, requesting that Appendix C be submitted to the Far Eastern Commission for policy decision.
subfiles.title: SWN-5354: Approval of SWNCC 302/2 on Excessive Concentrations of Economic Power in Japan

subfiles.about: Notifies holders of SWNCC 302/2 of amendments approved at the 56th SWNCC meeting and instructs substitution of revised pages.
subfiles.from: Secretariat, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee (H. W. Moseley, W. A. Schulgen, V. L. Lorance)
subfiles.summary: Records SWNCC approval of SWNCC 302/2 as amended at its 56th meeting and directs holders to substitute revised pages and burn superseded sheets.
subfiles.title: SWNCC Decision Amending SWNCC 302/2: Statement of U.S. Policy With Respect to Excessive Concentrations of Economic Power in Japan

subfiles.about: Instructs the U.S. Member to submit SWNCC 302/2 on excessive concentrations of economic power to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.from: Ernest A. Gross (for John H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Transmits Appendix C of SWNCC 302/2 on excessive concentrations of economic power, directing the U.S. Member to seek an FEC policy decision.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the United States Member, Far Eastern Commission Regarding SWNCC 302/2
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Extends an invitation to the Egyptian Government to send a three-member trade mission to Japan to negotiate cotton purchases and textile sales.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo
subfiles.summary: SCAP requests an invitation be extended to the Egyptian Government to send a three-man trade mission to negotiate raw cotton purchases and Japanese textile sales on a government-to-government basis.
subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram C 52370 from SCAP Proposing Egyptian Trade Mission to Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits inter-agency agreement directing the U.S. Member of the FEC to approve FEC 084/9 (SWNCC 302) with a duration amendment.
subfiles.from: H. W. Moseley (Secretary, SWNCC)
subfiles.summary: Requests the Secretary of State direct the U.S. FEC Member to approve FEC 084/9 with a terminating amendment.
subfiles.title: SWN-5365: Statement of the United States Position with Respect to Control of the Economic War Potential of Japan

subfiles.about: Directs the U.S. Member to approve FEC-084/9 regarding Japanese economic war potential with an agreed amendment limiting its duration.
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring (Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas)
subfiles.summary: Directs the U.S. Member of the FEC to approve FEC-084/9 regarding control of economic war potential with an amendment limiting applicability to January 1, 1949, or occupation end.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the United States Member, Far Eastern Commission on Approval of FEC-084/9 (SWNCC 302)
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Transmits SWNCC 302/5 containing a draft directive on assured Japanese production capacity levels.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Encloses for the Political Adviser's information a copy of SWNCC 302/5, 'Draft Directive Regarding Assured Production Capacity Levels for Japan'.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 49 to the United States Political Adviser to SCAP Transmitting SWNCC 302/5
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Discusses State Department assumption of military government, Locke's recommendations, and overcoming War Department opposition to engaging MacArthur on economic revival.
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring (Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas)
subfiles.summary: Hilldring notes that State's takeover of military government resolves Locke's concerns, but emphasizes the need for a vigorous Japanese economic program, urging discussions with Acheson to address Patterson's opposition and engage MacArthur.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Secretary of State on Japanese Economic Program and Civil Administration

subfiles.about: Critiques the proposed Japanese economic revival policy from a long-range geopolitical and diplomatic standpoint.
subfiles.from: Robert W. Barnett (Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Barnett argues that unilateral U.S. acceleration of Japanese recovery risks overturning fifty years of Asian diplomacy and alienating wartime allies. If full FEC concurrence cannot be secured, he recommends strictly limiting the revolving fund to short-term self-liquidating projects and dropping illusory promises of current reparations.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Promotion and Control of Japanese Economic Recovery
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin (Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs)

subfiles.about: Detailed critical study examining the economic, political, and strategic risks of U.S. plans to revive the Japanese economy and extract reparations from current production.
subfiles.from: Robert W. Barnett (Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Barnett provides an exhaustive critique of the State Department's proposed policy to 'crank up' the Japanese economy. He questions the feasibility of planned raw material imports from unstable Asian neighbors and warns that effective domestic consumption controls cannot be maintained without totalitarian methods or SCAP direct intervention. Furthermore, he cautions that prioritizing Japanese industrial revival over wartime allies like China and the Philippines will spark accusations of American economic colonialism, provoke Soviet alarm, and fail to produce promised reparations from current output. He urges adherence to SWNCC 52/7 principles, restricting assistance to self-liquidating commercial credits.
subfiles.title: Some Observations Regarding Promotion and Control of Japanese Economic Recovery
